title: Nowhere-dense closed subsets have smaller dimension
statement: Let X be a nonempty locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] of finite dimension d [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let Z be a closed subset of X that is nowhere dense. Then the Krull dimension of Z is strictly less than d.

source.place: Tag 02P2, conclusion from the nowhere-dense closed support; finite-dimensional Noetherian dimension argument

proof.text: If Z is empty, its Krull dimension is -infinity and the conclusion is immediate. Otherwise, let C be an irreducible component of Z. By [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], C is contained in an irreducible component W of X.

source.place: Tag 02P2, conclusion from the nowhere-dense closed support; irreducible-component containment from Topology Tag 004W

proof.text: By [lem-sc-locnoeth-components-locally-finite], the irreducible components of X are locally finite. Hence the union of the components other than W is closed near the generic point of W, and W has a nonempty open subset disjoint from that union. If C=W, this open subset lies in Z, contradicting that Z is nowhere dense. Therefore C is strictly contained in W. Every chain of irreducible closed subsets in C extends by W, so dim C + 1 <= dim W <= d.

source.place: Tag 02P2, finite-dimensional Noetherian dimension argument from a nowhere-dense closed support

proof.text: Taking the supremum over all irreducible components C of Z gives dim Z <= d - 1, hence dim Z < d. The same argument covers d=0: a nonempty C would force a strict chain in X, while the empty case was handled in step 1.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0052 (topology-lemma-Noetherian), with Tag 004W (topology-lemma-irreducible) for the component-cover input
